parameter_matrix.note: A part wins only if its operating Vin range strictly encompasses the counterpart on both ends.
Higher Vin,abs improves survivability against hot-plug and inductive bus spikes.
Tighter Vout tolerance improves ADC reference and digital rail margin.
Actual usable continuous Iout is also bounded by package θJA thermal derating.
Lower Iq directly extends sleep-mode battery life in always-on IoT/portable rails.
Lower dropout allows regulation deeper into Li-ion / 3.7 V discharge curves.

Higher PSRR attenuates upstream switching-converter ripple on analog/RF rails.
Critical for RF VCOs, low-noise ADCs, and precision sensor excitation.
Lower θJA yields lower junction temperature rise ΔTj = (Vin - Vout) × Iout × θJA.
Keep steady-state Tj at least 15–25 °C below Tj,max for production reliability.

engineering_verdict: TLV74333PDBVR (Texas Instruments, SOT-23-5) and TPS7A2033PDBVR (Texas Instruments, SOT-23-5) qualify as Level 1 Candidate Drop-In peers: all 5 pins share identical electrical roles, exposed-pad nets match (no EP), and thermal/voltage/temperature-grade margins remain aligned. Under a representative 5 V → 3.3 V rail at 150 mA (255 mW), estimated self-heating is ΔTj ≈ 58.2 °C on TLV74333PDBVR (θJA 228.4 °C/W) vs 47.7 °C on TPS7A2033PDBVR (θJA 187.1 °C/W), while quiescent draw spans a 5.2x ratio (34 µA (p.6) vs 6.5 µA (p.6)). Primary bench gotchas to watch: TLV74333PDBVR "EN Abs Max Strictly Capped at VIN + 0.3 V & No Internal EN Pulldown (Unlike TLV755P / TLV757P)" (p.5) and TPS7A2033PDBVR "Output Capacitor ESR Must Stay <= 100 mOhm (Avoid Tantalum/Electrolytic Caps)" (p.5). BOM decision: Choose TLV74333PDBVR when matching your existing Texas Instruments SOT-23-5 (DBV (SOT-23-5)) qualification and -40..125 °C grade; choose TPS7A2033PDBVR when battery sleep budget demands 6.5 µA Iq or lower package θJA (187.1 °C/W) is needed for thermal margin. Always verify Pin 1 orientation (TOP_VIEW p.4 vs TOP_VIEW p.4) and official datasheets on hardware prototypes prior to production.
